description: Health-state utilities used to calculate QALYs. Chronic utility is selected by Pettersson score; an acute event temporarily uses the lower of the chronic and acute-event utilities.
reference: ICER. Valoctocogene Roxaparvovec and Emicizumab for Hemophilia A: Effectiveness and Value. 2020.
Fischer K et al. The association of haemophilic arthropathy with health-related quality of life. Haemophilia. 2016;22(6):833-840. doi:10.1111/hae.13120.
Cohan D et al. Modeling Benefits, Costs, and Affordability of a Novel Gene Therapy in Hemophilia A. J Med Econ. 2022;25(1):182-193. doi:10.1080/13696998.2022.2033050.

pettersson_utility_thresholds.description: Inclusive lower bounds for the evidence-defined utility bands. PS 0 uses healthy; 1-4 early; 5-12 moderate; 13-21 severe; 22-39 advanced; and 40-79 end-stage.
pettersson_utility_thresholds.reference: Fischer et al. 2016 (doi:10.1111/hae.13120); PS 0 is separated using ICER/O'Hara evidence.

state_utilities.description: PS 0 is separated from early radiographic arthropathy so that a young, bleed-free patient on effective prophylaxis is not artificially capped at 0.82.
state_utilities.reference: See the citation and interpretation stored with each utility.

healthy.description: No established radiographic arthropathy: Pettersson score exactly 0. Intended for the young starting cohort. Acute bleeds are applied separately.
healthy.reference: ICER 2020, Table of health-state utilities: age 0-30 and Pettersson score 0 = 0.94, based on O'Hara et al. 2018 (doi:10.1186/s12955-018-0908-9).

uncertainty.description: Plausible range used for PSA; 0.82 is the ICER value for young patients with PS 1-27 and 1.00 is the utility ceiling.

mild_arthropathy.reference: Fischer et al. 2016 (doi:10.1111/hae.13120), reported for PS 0-4; PS 0 is separated in this model using ICER/O'Hara evidence.

uncertainty.description: Published standard deviation for the PS 0-4 group.

moderate_arthropathy.reference: Fischer et al. 2016 (doi:10.1111/hae.13120), as implemented in published haemophilia economic models.

severe_arthropathy.reference: Fischer et al. 2016 (doi:10.1111/hae.13120), as implemented in published haemophilia economic models.

advanced_arthropathy.reference: Fischer et al. 2016 (doi:10.1111/hae.13120), as implemented in published haemophilia economic models.

end_stage_arthropathy.description: Pettersson score 40-78; score 79 is capped into this final model band.
end_stage_arthropathy.reference: Fischer et al. 2016 (doi:10.1111/hae.13120), as implemented in published haemophilia economic models.

bleeding.description: Temporary utility during a treated non-target-joint bleed.
bleeding.reference: Neufeld EJ et al. Effect of acute bleeding on daily quality of life assessments in patients with congenital hemophilia with inhibitors. Value Health. 2012;15(6):916-925. doi:10.1016/j.jval.2012.05.005; uncertainty bounds follow Cohan et al. 2022.

hemarthrosis.description: Temporary utility during a treated target-joint bleed/hemarthrosis.
hemarthrosis.reference: Mazza G et al. Value Health. 2016;19(7):A608. doi:10.1016/j.jval.2016.09.1420; implemented as 0.66 non-target bleed utility minus 0.12 target-joint decrement in Cohan et al. 2022.

uncertainty.description: Symmetric plausible range around the modelled 0.54 estimate; tested because the source is a conference abstract and the value is derived.

intracranial_hemorrhage.description: Utility for a major nonfatal intracranial hemorrhage. The current simulation applies it during the acute ICH state week only.
intracranial_hemorrhage.reference: Hogg K et al. Preferences for treatments to prevent venous thromboembolism after total hip or knee arthroplasty. JAMA Intern Med. 2013;173(8):612-620. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2013.563.

uncertainty.description: Published median 0.15 and IQR 0.00-0.65; represented approximately as a triangular PSA distribution.

non_ich_major_bleeding.description: Temporary utility during an acute non-ICH major bleed.
reference: Hogg K et al. JAMA Intern Med. 2013;173(8):612-620. doi:10.1001/jamainternmed.2013.563: standard-gamble utility approximately 0.65 for one week of gastrointestinal bleeding.

National Clinical Guideline Centre. Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: Management. NICE Clinical Guideline 141, full guideline, 2012: economic analysis used utility 0.45 while hospitalized and 0.78 at home. https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg141/evidence/full-guideline-pdf-186534541
Base case 0.55 is the prespecified midpoint between these two estimates.
